papers.title: Automating Financial Statement Audits with Large Language Models
papers.status: arXiv v1, 14 June 2025; no conference acceptance verified

source_claims.scale: 371 source statements from 124 collected images; 1,484 single-error variants and 371 multiple-error variants (paper Dataset Statistics).
source_claims.task: General judgment, error identification, explanation/resolution, standards citation, and table revision.
source_claims.evidence: Public financial statement images converted to text; GPT-generated transaction evidence and error injections with reported human review.
source_claims.evaluation: 150 sampled cases per evaluated split; exact matches for several tasks, BERTScore explanations, retriever-based Top-1/Top-3 citation scoring, BLEU table revision, and overall success.

licenses.paper: arXiv perpetual non-exclusive license; not a data redistribution license
licenses.data: Not verified; linked repository license endpoint returned HTTP 404

limitations: Synthetic evidence and mutations can permit shortcuts; reported scores do not measure independent paragraph applicability.
Citation Top-1 retrieval matching is not the proposed full paragraph exact-match or entailment metric.
Do not repeat the local claim of 1,856 real source statements: the paper reports 371 source statements.
papers.positioning: Use as a legacy control, not as proof that the new benchmark is valid. The user's Automating Financial Statements and AuditBench references identify the same work.
papers.verification: Primary-source claims checked; experiments and full dataset contents not independently reproduced in this review.

source_claims.scale: 1,102 instances: FinSM 330, FinRE 440, FinMR 332; average 34,338.64 tokens (v3 Table 4).
source_claims.task: Financial semantic matching, relationship extraction, and mathematical reasoning over XBRL.
source_claims.evidence: Real filing sub-documents and US-GAAP taxonomy; labels deterministically derived from DQC messages; GPT-4o-mini assists parsing rather than deciding labels (v3 §3.3.1).
source_claims.evaluation: 13 evaluated models; retrieval metrics for FinSM, relation classification metrics for FinRE; FinMR numerical accuracy using an LLM judge with structural/extraction/calculation error diagnostics.

licenses.code: Not verified; repository license endpoint returned HTTP 404

limitations: DQC consistency violations do not establish fraudulent intent or comprehensive accounting-standard compliance.
FinMR public cases are positive flagged cases; add independently reviewed clean controls for false-alarm measurement.
Dataset card author/title metadata lags v3; use the paper metadata for bibliography.
papers.positioning: Closest reusable structured-data control; use public FinMR for regression checks and fresh blinded cases for the principal result.
papers.verification: Primary-source claims checked; experiments and full dataset contents not independently reproduced in this review.

papers.title: AUDITFLOW: Executable Symbolic Environments for Structured Financial Reporting Verification
papers.status: arXiv v1, 2 June 2026; no conference acceptance verified

source_claims.scale: 67 FinMR-derived instances across 47 tickers; 22 DQC.US.0015, 24 DQC.US.0117, 21 DQC.US.0126; 29 10-K and 38 10-Q filings.
source_claims.task: Targeted structured reporting verification; output audit verdict, expected value, evidence trail and trustworthiness.
source_claims.evidence: Independently downloaded EDGAR XBRL packages and taxonomy releases; static taxonomy plus dynamic filing graph; typed deterministic tools; two junior agents and senior arbitration.

licenses.data: Uses FinAuditing-derived data; verify provenance for any redistributed derivative

Only 67 sampled cases and three DQC families; paper percentages cannot be compared to a new dataset directly.
Cap on tool steps differs from controlled evidence availability with heterogeneous acquisition costs.
papers.positioning: Required closest-method baseline. Proposed extension tests costed acquisition, sufficient evidence and standards applicability under matched inputs, rather than merely adding agents.

paper_reported_metrics.name: Joint accuracy after removing deterministic checks

papers.title: AuditFraudBench: Benchmarking Audit Judgment in Detecting Fraudulent Misstatements
papers.status: arXiv v1, 6 June 2026; comments explicitly Work in progress

source_claims.scale: 84 companies and 84 AAER cases; 143 10-K, 136 10-Q, 16 20-F; task counts 34 / 294 / 295 (Table 1).
source_claims.task: Profit source attribution, misleading narrative detection, fraud-pattern classification.
source_claims.evidence: Original/restated filings, structured financials, MD&A and SEC AAER enforcement records aligned to misconduct mechanisms.
source_claims.evaluation: Accuracy, precision/recall/F1 and ROUGE conditional/gated explanation metrics; GPT, DeepSeek and Qwen variants up to 32B.

licenses.data: No downloadable dataset license verified from supplied primary page

Restatements and AAERs are outcome evidence; keep them evaluator-only when assessing contemporaneous fraud discovery.
papers.positioning: Supports enforcement-grounded case selection, while motivating balanced controls, investigation-time evidence cutoffs and process scoring.

paper_reported_metrics.name: Task 1 attribution classification accuracy (all positive instances)

papers.title: FinancialAuditBench: Benchmark Construction under Differential Privacy Using Real-World Priors
papers.status: arXiv v1 submitted 26 September 2026; no conference acceptance verified

source_claims.scale: 90 workpaper-completion/review tasks; six synthetic engagements, average 179 files; over 1,100 auditor development/review hours.
source_claims.task: Staff-level audit workpaper completion and review across manufacturing and staffing engagements.
source_claims.evidence: Computational graph (~250 nodes, ~1,000 edges) generates consistent binders; differentially private aggregate historical priors; CPA-authored/reviewed reference workpapers and rubrics.
source_claims.evaluation: Eleven frontier models; strict rubric pass, partial credit, cost/time and eight-attempt reliability; bounded rubric coverage is explicitly acknowledged.

licenses.code: MIT verified via GitHub license API

limitations: Already supplies internally consistent multi-document evidence, a generation graph and auditor-designed rubrics; avoid claiming those features as firsts.

Published mean Opus cost is $3.30 per task; reproducing 90 tasks would exceed the user's entire pilot budget before cheaper baselines.
papers.positioning: Most important new comparison. Differentiate a modest openly reproducible acquisition-and-citation benchmark, not a larger synthetic binder generator or unsupported privacy claim.

paper_reported_metrics.name: Mean cost per task in USD

No frontier-produced labels or frontier-as-judge for the same frontier-comparator cases.
Report actual model version, API costs, latency and caching; literature metrics are context only.
Company/filing/event-disjoint splitting and grouped uncertainty; 5–10 companies remain a pilot, not broad population representation.
Separate annotation validity, detection, evidence sufficiency, citation retrieval, citation applicability, calibration and cost.
